entities.name: PMID:27515722
observations: Drug and Alcohol Dependence (2016) study of substance use disorders among U.S. probationers and parolees using National Survey on Drug Use and Health data from 2002–2014.
SUD prevalence among probationers/parolees was four to nine times higher than among people not under supervision and changed little over the study period.
Outcomes included alcohol, illicit-drug, marijuana/hashish, and combined alcohol–illicit-drug abuse and dependence; logistic regression assessed correlates.

entities.name: Stable high SUD burden
observations: Among U.S. probationers and parolees, SUD levels were high and relatively constant from 2002 through 2014; levels were four to nine times those of people not under supervision.
Alcohol abuse/dependence prevalence was approximately two to six times that of marijuana and other illicit-drug abuse/dependence.

entities.name: SUD correlates
observations: Abuse outcomes correlated with age, gender, race/ethnicity, education, income, risk propensity, crime/violence measures, and comorbid substance abuse.
Dependence had similar correlates and additionally included employment and mental-health treatment.

entities.name: Probation prevalence estimates
observations: In the retrieved study passage, probationer estimates versus non-probationers were: alcohol abuse 13.0% vs 3.8%; illicit-drug abuse 2.3% vs 0.3%; combined alcohol/illicit-drug abuse 1.1% vs 0.2%; marijuana/hashish abuse 3.4% vs 0.5%.

Dependence estimates were alcohol 14.8% vs 3.2%; illicit drugs 7.6% vs 0.9%; combined alcohol/illicit drugs 4.1% vs 0.4%; marijuana/hashish 5.5% vs 0.9%. These figures were labeled probationer-specific in the retrieved passage.
